diagrams.caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 1: Rear Combination Lamps, Cargo Area, Fuel Delivery, Defogger, and Center Console Harness
diagrams.description: Full high-resolution electrical schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z rear body, tail lighting, fuel pump, fuel gauge sending unit, rear window defogger grid, auto antenna, audio speakers, center console switches, and harness connectors C-1 through C-10.
measurements_and_specs: Fuel tank sender resistance: approx. 10 to 80 ohms (Empty ~80Ω, Full ~10Ω)
Rear window defogger current draw: 12-15A (approx. 1 ohm total grid resistance)
Stop lamp bulbs: 12V 21W / 32CP
Tail lamp bulbs: 12V 5W / 3CP
Turn signal bulbs: 12V 21W / 32CP
Back-up lamp bulbs: 12V 21W / 32CP
diagrams.mechanic_notes: All rear exterior lamps share the common body ground point in the rear hatch quarter panel; corroded or loose ground lugs cause dim lamps or cross-backfeeding into turn signal circuits.

diagrams.caption: Rear Exterior Lighting, Fuel Pump, and Tank Sending Unit Sub-Circuit
diagrams.description: Close-up detail of the rear lighting harness, license lamps, fuel pump power feed, and fuel level sender connections.
measurements_and_specs: Fuel pump operating voltage: 12V (draws approx. 3.0-4.5A)
Fuel level gauge resistance: 10 ohms (full) to 80 ohms (empty)
wiring_and_connections: G: Turn Signal RH & Fuel Pump feed
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Verify fuel pump dedicated ground lug bolted to inner wheel arch frame to avoid intermittent engine stall under vibration.

diagrams.caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 2: Combination Meter, Steering Column Switches, Under-Dash Fuse Box, Relay Bracket, and HVAC System
diagrams.description: Comprehensive schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z dashboard electrical wiring including the combination meter cluster (volts, fuel, temp, oil, tach, speedo, clock), steering column combination switch contact matrices, ignition switch, 12-circuit fuse block, relay bracket, and heater/AC controls.
measurements_and_specs: Fuse ratings: 10A (x6), 15A (x2), 20A (x4)
Seat belt warning timer interval: 4-8 seconds
Tachometer calibration: 4 pulses per 2 revolutions (6-cylinder 4-stroke)
Water temperature sender resistance: approx. 70-90Ω at 60°C (140°F), 20-30Ω at 100°C (212°F)
Oil pressure sender resistance: approx. 10-15Ω at 0 psi, 80-90Ω at 60 psi
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When troubleshooting no-start or dead instrument clusters, inspect the ignition switch solder joints and the multi-pin connector C-6 for burnt pins caused by high current draw.

diagrams.caption: Under-Dash Fuse Box, Ignition Switch, and Relay Bracket Sub-Circuit
diagrams.description: Focused schematic showing the under-dash 12-circuit fuse box power distribution, ignition switch contact assignments, and relay bracket module pinouts.
measurements_and_specs: Fuse box continuous rating: 12V 10A-20A glass barrel fuses (SFE/AGC type)
Ignition switch rating: 30A continuous at 12V
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Glass fuse clips in the 280Z fuse box are prone to corrosion and tension loss, causing voltage drop to EFI and ignition circuits.

diagrams.caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 3: Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) ECU, Injector Harness, Dropping Resistor Bank, Air Flow Meter, and Power Distribution
diagrams.description: Complete schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) circuitry showing the 35-pin ECU connector pinout, dropping resistor bank, 6 fuel injectors, cold start valve, thermotime switch, air regulator, throttle valve switch, air flow meter, battery, and fusible links.
measurements_and_specs: Dropping resistor individual branch resistance: 5.6 to 6.4 ohms
Fuel injector coil resistance: 2.0 to 3.0 ohms (low impedance)
Water temperature sensor resistance: 2.1 to 2.9 kΩ at 20°C (68°F); 0.27 to 0.38 kΩ at 80°C (176°F)
Air regulator heater coil resistance: approx. 70 to 80 ohms
Thermotime switch opening temperature: approx. 35°C (95°F); max cranking duration: 8-12 seconds
Air flow meter potentiometer resistance (pins 8-9): approx. 180 to 220 ohms
Fusible link capacities: Brown (0.3mm² / approx. 30A), Green (0.5mm² / approx. 40A), Black (1.25mm² / approx. 80A)
wiring_and_connections: BY (Starter cranking trigger: Pin 4 & cold start)
G (AFM fuel pump safety switch / injector power)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: A poor ground connection at the intake manifold engine earth cluster is the #1 cause of bizarre EFI malfunctions, rich surging, or injector failure to fire.

diagrams.caption: EFI Control Unit, Dropping Resistor, and Injector Bank Sub-Circuit
diagrams.description: High-density detail of the 35-pin Bosch L-Jetronic ECU pin connections, dropping resistor connections, and 6-cylinder injector firing lines.
measurements_and_specs: Total injector resistance per cylinder: approx. 8.5Ω (2.5Ω injector + 6.0Ω resistor)
Injector pulse width: 2.0 to 9.0 milliseconds depending on load/temperature
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Never connect 12V directly across the fuel injectors without the dropping resistor in series; doing so will immediately fry the delicate low-impedance injector solenoid windings.

diagrams.caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 4: Alternator, IC Regulator, Starter Motor, Electronic Distributor, Ignition Coil, Front Lighting, and Relay Bracket
diagrams.description: Comprehensive schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z front engine compartment electrical system including alternator charging circuit, solid-state IC regulator, starter motor cranking circuit, ballast resistor, high-energy ignition coil, electronic distributor, front lighting, and under-hood diagnostic check connector.
components: Relay Bracket (EFI Main, Fuel Pump, A/C, Inhibitor)
measurements_and_specs: Alternator regulated voltage: 14.0 to 14.7V at 2,500 RPM
Alternator maximum output: 60A at 12V
Starter motor no-load current: less than 90A at 11V (over 4,000 RPM)
Ballast resistor total resistance: approx. 1.5 to 1.7 ohms
Ignition coil primary winding resistance: approx. 1.0 to 1.3 ohms
Ignition coil secondary winding resistance: approx. 8.0 to 12.0 kΩ
Distributor magnetic pickup stator resistance: approx. 600 to 800 ohms
Firing order: 1 - 5 - 3 - 6 - 2 - 4 (clockwise distributor rotation)
Spark plug gap: 0.8 to 0.9 mm (0.031 to 0.035 in)
wiring_and_connections: WR: Alternator BAT output / Battery feed
WB: Alternator field coil / IC regulator F
Y: Alternator neutral stator tap / IC regulator N
YW: IC regulator L terminal / Charge lamp
W: IC regulator S terminal (battery sense)
BR: Starter terminal R ballast bypass line
BW: Switched ignition 12V to ballast resistor
L: Ignition coil negative / TIU switching / Tach
G / R: Distributor magnetic pickup stator twisted pair
GB: Horn relay output to dual horns
YL: Oil pressure sending unit signal
YW: Water temperature sending unit signal
diagrams.mechanic_notes: The ballast bypass line (Black/Red wire from starter terminal R to coil positive) is essential for cold starting; if disconnected, the engine will crank vigorously but will only catch or fire as the key is released back to the ON position.

diagrams.caption: Alternator, IC Regulator, Starter, and Ignition Sub-Circuit
diagrams.description: High-density detail of the alternator charging circuit with solid-state IC regulator, starter motor solenoid wiring, ballast resistor, high-tension ignition coil, and distributor.
measurements_and_specs: Regulated charging voltage: 14.0 - 14.7V
Ballast resistor: 1.6 ohms
Coil primary: 1.1 ohms
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use the 6-pin Check Connector to test charging and ignition signals directly with a multimeter without puncturing harness insulation.

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine cranks vigorously but will not fire or start; catches momentarily only when ignition key is released from START to ON
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Open circuit in ballast bypass circuit: Black/Red (BR) wire from starter solenoid terminal 'R' to ignition coil (+) post is broken, disconnected, or starter solenoid internal auxiliary contact is oxidized.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check continuity on Black/Red wire between starter terminal R and ignition coil (+) terminal. Inspect starter solenoid auxiliary terminal; verify 12V is present at coil (+) during key crank.

troubleshooting.symptom: Fuel pump does not run during engine cranking or running
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty Air Flow Meter fuel pump interlock switch (pins 34-35), defective Fuel Pump Relay, blown 20A fuse, or corroded rear fuel pump ground eyelet.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check continuity between AFM terminals 34 and 35 when flap is manually deflected. Check for 12V at Green wire at fuel pump connector C-2 during cranking. Clean dedicated fuel pump ground connection in rear spare tire well.

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine starts cold and dies immediately; extreme hesitation and black exhaust smoke upon acceleration
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective Water Temperature Sensor or open circuit in harness wires Red/Yellow (RY) or Black (B) to ECU pins 13 and 16, causing computer to assume coolant temperature is -40°C.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Measure resistance across ECU pins 13 and 16 at the 35-pin connector. Normal cold reading at 20°C is ~2.5 kΩ, dropping to ~300Ω at normal operating temperature. Replace sensor if open circuit.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake warning light in combination meter remains illuminated continuously with handbrake fully released
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Master cylinder brake fluid level is low, fluid level float switch stuck down, parking brake lever switch bent/shorted to ground, or Warning Lamp Check Relay stuck closed.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Inspect brake fluid levels in front and rear master cylinder reservoirs. Disconnect fluid level switch harness; if light extinguishes, top off fluid or replace reservoir cap float assembly. Inspect handbrake switch contact.

troubleshooting.symptom: Intermittent windshield wipers inoperative, but Low and High speeds function normally
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty Intermittent Wiper Amplifier on relay bracket, defective wiper switch INT contact (Blue/Red wire), or missing ground connection on amplifier Black lead.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check for switched 12V on Blue wire at Intermittent Wiper Amplifier. Verify ground on Black wire. Check continuity of Blue/Red wire between steering column wiper switch and amplifier.

troubleshooting.symptom: Battery discharges overnight or undercharges; red CHARGE indicator lamp does not illuminate with key ON before starting
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Burnt-out charge warning bulb in speedometer, blown meter fuse (Fuse 6, 10A), or disconnected Yellow/White wire at IC regulator terminal 'L'. (Excitation current through bulb is required to initialize alternator charging field).
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace defective charge warning bulb in combination meter. Verify 12V on Black/White wire to IC regulator terminal IG and inspect Yellow/White wire continuity between meter and regulator.
